label: Utterance-level sound properties
summary: Utterance-level sound properties is what prosody refers to: the sonic characteristics that apply to whole utterances rather than individual sounds or words. Examples include intonation, stress, and pitch. It is a foundational concept for anyone working with SSML in voice and conversation design.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike introduces prosody as the practical core of SSML work, framing it as the main layer conversation designers manipulate when tagging speech. She situates it within a broader primer on speech concepts, using it to draw a clear contrast between the properties of whole utterances and those of individual words or sounds, and signals that it will be a recurring concept in subsequent parts of the series.
open_questions: The primer is explicitly part 1, so how prosody interacts with other speech properties in SSML practice is left to be developed in later parts.
The passage mentions stress as a prosodic property but does not explain it further, leaving its practical implications for voice design unaddressed.
